newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - DLR VOLS STEADY AS SPOT MOVES CALM DOWN.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - DLR VOLS STEADY AS SPOT MOVES CALM DOWN.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/mark and dollar/yen options were mostly steady across the board as the market calmed down after a flurry of vols buying on Monday following spot dollar's spectacular fall on Friday.
But traders were still on edge after the dollar plunged by more than four pfennings and four yen just before the weekend.

"Yen vols have calmed down and dollar/Europe vols are in a range for the time being. But the market is nervous, and we need to see more days of range-trading in the spot for volatilities to come down," said one trader at a German bank in London.

One-month dollar/mark vols were quoted at 11.00/40 percent at 1130 GMT against their late Monday European level of 10.90/11.20. The German bank trader noted sellers at 11.50 percent and buyers at 11.20.
Spot dollar/mark was firm at Europe's midsession after the Bundesbank decided to keep its securities repurchase tender rate at a fixed 3.0 percent.

At the same time, the Bundesbank had stayed silent concerning future money market activity, keeping alive the speculation that it might switch to a variable rate repo next week and allow rates to rise, and this was capping dollar/mark.
It was at 1.8634/39 marks against 1.8545/55 late on Monday.
Risk reversals were biased in favour of mark puts, the same as on Monday, with the 25-delta risk reversal at 0.2/0.5 against yesterday's 0.1/0.3.

Dollar/yen vols cooled down as well after a sharp rise in one-month vols and a slight easing further out on Monday. One-month vols fell to 11.60/90 percent from 12.10/40 percent in late European trade on Monday, while one-year was quoted at 11.55/75 against 11.70/90.
Yen calls were still in demand though less so than on Monday, with the risk reversal at 0.0/0.3 against 0.2/0.5 yesterday.
Meanwhile, traders said sterling vols picked up after a soft start to the day, adding that volatilities were tracking moves in spot trade.

"There was some selling off of sterling volatility at the beginning of the day, but the increase in spot activity during the day has pushed vols back up a bit," said one trader at a Swiss bank in London.

Spot sterling/mark had started the day soft but rose markedly after data showing British retail price inflation was at its highest in nearly two years. The pound was at 2.9543/53 marks against 2.9470/80 in late European trade on Monday.
One-month sterling/mark vols were at 11.90/12.40 percent against late Monday levels of 11.70/20. Risk reversals favoured sterling puts at 0.3/0.8 against 0.4/0.9.
